data.title: WSJ Tech Council Summit: CVS Uses Surveys of AI Bots for Message Testing, Market Research
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

When CVS Health looks to roll out a new product, they have a new source of data at their proposal: a set of 150,000 artificial-intelligence simulations, or copies, of its real customers, ready to be surveyed at the click of a button.

The company has partnered with Simile, a startup building AI models based on real human behavior. It has used Simile's tech to build digital "twins" of clinicians and providers to run message-testing surveys far faster than traditional surveys of humans.

"We've introduced biosimilars which we think are clinically as effective and actually represent cost savings for our consumers, but we have to get those in the market and convince consumers to adopt them," Sri Narasimhan, CVS Health's vice president of enterprise customer experience & insights, said Monday at The Wall Street Journal's Technology Council Summit.

"We went and asked a bunch of clinicians and twins of clinicians, 'What's the information you would need to recommend a biosimilar to your patient?'" Narasimhan said, noting that the survey led to recommendations around clinical evidence and lead time. "We actually adopted it and we saw the outcome. We saw an increase in the prescription and it was a great outcome for our patients, great outcome for the providers as the clinical outcomes were better as well."

Joon Sung Park, Simile's co-founder and chief executive, said the company's models are based on data from tens of millions of real people, and can help businesses make predictions about human behavior and generate better outcomes.

"Simulation is a tool for creating a multiverse of possibility to basically chart out what is the golden path that is the most likely for you to actually get to the particular outcome that you want," Park said.

Using AI simulations has allowed CVS Health to run survey-based research around ten times faster than traditional human surveys, with lower levels of noise and human bias, CVS Health Chief Experience and Technology Officer Tilak Mandadi said.

Narasimhan added that the company tested simulation-based and traditional surveys against each other and found that the twins have a roughly 90% to 95% accuracy rate.

"If you're looking at, 'Hey, we're introducing something, we're piloting something, we want to see what people will make and how their perception will change,' that's where I think simulation has a really big role in disrupting traditional research methods, insights, market research, and things like that," Narasimhan said.

data.title: EPA to Roll Back Power-Plant Emission Rules — WSJ
data.description:
By Jennifer Hiller

The Environmental Protection Agency said Monday that it would repeal some carbon dioxide emission rules for power plants, part of a broader effort to curtail the agency's role in regulating climate change.

The move would unwind two key policies of the Obama and Biden eras around carbon emissions.

The first would reverse Biden-era policies to crack down on pollution from coal plants and newly built natural-gas-fired power plants. The other concerns the EPA's broader authority to regulate climate pollution under the Clean Air Act, which could prevent future administrations from regulating power-plant emissions.

EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin called Monday's actions "the largest deregulatory action for the United States power sector in American history."

The agency acted in February to rescind the Obama-era endangerment finding, which classifies six greenhouse gases as a threat to public health and welfare.

That finding had provided the legal underpinning to climate rules that limited emissions from power plants and tightened fuel-economy standards for vehicles under the Clean Air Act. But the administration's rule changes earlier this year focused on the autos sector and tailpipe emissions, not the power industry.

"Today's proposal states the Clean Air Act does not give us the authority to regulate power-plant emissions based on climate change," Zeldin said at a G-20 Ministerial Meeting on Energy Abundance in Houston. "At EPA, we follow a very simple principle. If Congress didn't authorize it, EPA shouldn't be doing it."

A legal fight is already under way and is expected to grow.

The power industry had pushed back against Biden administration rules that would have required power plants to implement carbon capture and storage technology, or switch to hydrogen fuel from natural gas. New plants that didn't comply with one of those options wouldn't have been able to operate at full capacity.

The rules didn't apply to existing gas plants, the backbone of the nation's power supply. But many new gas-fired power plants are now proposed to meet surging demand for electricity for AI data centers.

The rule was considered especially difficult for coal-fired power plants, as they are already more complex and costly to operate than natural-gas plants, and have had a hard time competing in the market against gas and renewables.

Jim Matheson, chief executive of the National Rural Electric Cooperative Association, called the Biden-era rule "unachievable."

"It also exacerbates the pressures facing America's electric grid by forcing critical existing power plants into early retirement and severely restricting the operation of new natural gas plants," Matheson said.

Attorney Alex Bond of Baker Botts, who previously worked at the EPA office of general counsel, said there are several legal cases at play around the Clean Air Act, the endangerment finding and the EPA's climate authority.

"Ultimately this has the 'Supreme Court' written all over it," Bond said. "The question is just what issue is going to go up to the Supreme Court, and when are we going to get

any type resolution on what that authority looks like?"

The move to unwind EPA regulations has been seen as a victory for the fossil-fuel industry, which for years has pushed back against federal climate regulations. Since taking office, President Trump has framed fossil fuels as vital to economic and national security, and he has argued that increased reliance on them would help lower energy prices.

His administration has ordered several older fossil-fuel-fired power plants that were scheduled for retirement to continue operating under emergency orders. Last week, though, a federal appeals court struck down one of those orders to keep a coal-fired power plant in Michigan running past its planned retirement.

Write to Jennifer Hiller at jennifer.hiller@wsj.com

data.title: Soybean barge basis mixed, corn unchanged
data.description:
Basis bids for soybeans shipped by barge to the U.S. Gulf Coast were mixed on Monday, with values for loadings in the winter ticking higher amid strengthening demand from top soybean importer China, traders said.

  • The U.S. Department of Agriculture reported that 672,759 metric tons of U.S. soybeans were inspected for export in the latest week, topping a range of trade expectations for 300,000 to 600,000 tons.

  • Traders were optimistic about Chinese export demand for U.S. soy ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's upcoming visit to Washington.

  • China's total U.S. soybean buying has clocked in at nearly half of the 25 million tons the White House said Beijing had committed to annually through 2028.

  • Railroad fuel surcharges on U.S. grain shipments have more than doubled over the past year, rippling through the farm belt and raising transportation costs as many farmers also struggle with higher production costs.

  • The average fuel surcharge rate on grain shipments climbed to 48 cents a mile per rail car in the second week of September, up 153% compared with the weighted average a year earlier, according to U.S. Department of Agriculture data. Railroads use surcharges to recover most of what they have paid for fuel and combine them with long-haul freight rates.

  • The National Oilseed Processors Association is due to release its August U.S. crush report on Tuesday. Analysts polled by Reuters, on average, expect last month's crush to dip to 211.553 million bushels, a three-month low.

  • CIF corn basis bids were mostly flat while CIF soybean bids and offers were mixed.

data.title: U.S. Sanctions Russian Bank in Latest Target for Campaign Against Iran — WSJ
data.description:
By Dylan Tokar

The Treasury Department on Monday identified Russia's second-largest financial institution, VTB Bank, as a key financial node for Iran's Islamic Republic and put further sanctions on the bank.

The new sanctions on VTB are a bid to pressure international partners to cut off dealings with it, according to people familiar with the matter. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has repeatedly threatened secondary sanctions against foreign companies that help Iran to evade U.S. economic restrictions.

Bessent, who announced a maximum pressure campaign against Iran dubbed Operation Economic Outcast last month, previewed the latest sanctions on Friday without naming the target. "We are just going to continue with this process until everyone stops dealing with this regime," he said.

VTB Bank didn't immediately return a request for comment.

The immediate impact of the new sanctions is unclear. VTB was already put under U.S. sanctions in 2022 in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and the pre-existing sanctions prohibit any U.S. person or institution from dealing with VTB.

The Russian bank has continued to provide a major lifeline to Iran despite those sanctions, according to U.S. officials. VTB provides clearing accounts to the Central Bank of Iran and a number of sanctioned Iranian banks, allowing for the easy exchange of Iranian rials and Russian rubles, the people familiar with the matter said.

VTB has more than a thousand branches around the globe and a notable presence in India, the people said. It has moved to increase its presence in Iran and helped transfer billions in frozen Iranian assets, the Treasury said Monday.

The Treasury in recent weeks has inched toward more aggressively deploying its sanctions capabilities against Iran, including by moving to cut off banks in Turkey and the U.A.E that officials said help the regime evade sanctions.

Billions of dollars in Iran-related transactions move through U.S. banks each year thanks to a century-old network that allows banks in different countries to seamlessly exchange and transfer currencies. U.S. banks hold a special position in that system because of the importance of the U.S. dollar.

Cutting foreign banks off from the U.S. dollar accounts can hurt the dollar and have collateral consequences for U.S. allies and the global financial system more broadly, which has forced the Trump administration and its predecessors to move with caution when targeting adversaries such as Iran.

The Treasury last month moved to sever the Emirati branch of a state-owned Egyptian bank from its correspondent accounts at several large U.S. banks. The action stopped short of imposing full secondary sanctions on Banque Misr UAE.

So far, the Treasury Department hasn't targeted China, Iran's top trading partner, which has raised questions about how far it can go in squeezing the regime.

Miad Maleki, a senior Treasury official until last year, who now works at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said the move against VTB was likely also a warning to China. Maleki said that VTB's Shanghai branch is the only Russian bank inside China's payment system and it has become a key artery for Russian-Chinese trade.

By placing VTB under Iran sanctions, Treasury is telling Chinese banks that "their VTB business is now Iran business and, in this environment, Iran exposure is something no bank in Shanghai, Hong Kong or Mumbai wants on its books," he said.

China's leader Xi Jinping is due in Washington to meet President Trump this month.

Write to Dylan Tokar at dylan.tokar@wsj.com

data.title: Ocean Power Initiates Strategic Review Following Leadership Changes
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Ocean Power Technologies said it initiated a strategic alternatives review following its quarterly results and a leadership shakeup.

The maker of ocean products said Monday that its board initiated the review to identify opportunities to increase growth, expand market access and strengthen the company's financial position.

Bowen is serving as financial adviser and no timetable has been established for the review.

The news came as Ocean Power said fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 44% to $1.7 million. Its loss widened to $10.5 million from $7.4 million the year before, with the per-share loss remaining stable at $1.28.

Earlier on Monday, Ocean Power announced leadership changes including the departure of Chief Executive Philipp Stratmann. The company's previous chief executive, Tracy Pagliara, will come in as acting CEO.

Shares were down 4% to $2.62 in after-hours trading. Shares ended the regular session down 15% at $2.73.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

(the "Selling Shareholder"), a company indirectly owned by funds managed by Oaktree Capital Management, L.P. and its affiliates. The Selling Shareholder expects to grant the underwriter a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 1,350,000 (one million three hundred fifty thousand) Class A common shares offered in this offering. The offering is subject to market and other conditions, and there can be no assurance as to whether or when the offering may be completed.

The Selling Shareholder beneficially owns approximately 20% of the Company's Class A common shares prior to this offering. The Company is not selling any Class A common shares and will not receive any proceeds from the sale of the Company's Class A common shares by the Selling Shareholder.

J.P. Morgan Securities LLC is acting as sole underwriter for the offering. The underwriter intends to offer the Company's Class A common shares to the public at a fixed price, which may be changed at any time without notice. The offering will be made only by means of a prospectus supplement and accompanying base prospectus related to the offering, copies of which may be obtained, when available, from J.P. data.title: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation Arranges $53 Million Build-to-Rent Refinance in Northwest Arkansas
data.description:
Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation (MMCC), a leading provider of commercial real estate capital markets financing solutions, has arranged $53 million in refinancing for The Grove, a build-to-rent (BTR) multifamily property in Rogers, Arkansas.

John Brickson, managing director in MMCC’s Dallas office, represented a joint venture between Brittenum Group and Realty Capital Partners in securing and structuring three-year, nonrecourse financing.

“This financing repaid the borrower’s construction loan ahead of maturity, giving the borrower time to season the rent roll and position the property for a successful sale,” said Brickson. “The Grove has been very well received in the market and has exceptional resident demographics, with median household income of nearly $100,000 among the existing resident base. The property is one of the largest BTR communities by unit count in the Northwest Arkansas region and one of the few projects offering fully detached, single-family-style homes.”

Built in 2024, this 235-unit Class A community is 94.5% occupied and consists of 123 detached two-story, single-family-style cottages and 112 attached townhome-style residences. Amenities include a resort-style pool, 24-hour fitness center, golf simulator, package lockers, community clubhouse with co-working offices and a community kitchen, and a pickleball court.

About Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation

Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation (MMCC) is a subsidiary of Marcus & Millichap (NYSE: MMI), a leading commercial real estate investment services firm with offices throughout the United States and Canada. MMCC provides commercial real estate capital markets financing solutions, including debt, mezzanine financing, preferred and joint venture equity, sponsor equity, loan sales and consultative and due diligence services. In 2025, MMCC closed 1,659 transactions totaling $11.9 billion. To learn more, please visit: marcusmillichap.com/financing.

About Brittenum Group

The Brittenum Group is a privately held, fully integrated residential development and construction firm focused on the development of single family, townhome, and build-to-rent communities throughout Northwest Arkansas. Through its affiliated entities, including Brittenum Residential, Brittenum Construction, and Precision Sitework, the firm provides comprehensive in-house capabilities spanning development, construction management, sitework, and project delivery. The Brittenum Group has established a strong presence throughout the Northwest Arkansas market with communities located across Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, Springdale, Prairie Grove, and surrounding submarkets. The firm is led by Chief Executive Officer Jon Brittenum Jr, an experienced developer with over 30 years of industry expertise across land development, construction, and strategic growth. For more information, please visit www.brittenumresidential.com

About Marcus & Millichap, Inc. (NYSE:MMI)

Marcus & Millichap, Inc. is a leading brokerage firm specializing in commercial real estate investment sales, financing, research and advisory services, with offices throughout the United States and Canada. Marcus & Millichap closed 8,818 transactions with a sales volume of $50.8 billion in 2025. At year-end, the company had 1,808 investment sales and financing professionals in more than 80 offices providing investment brokerage and financing services to commercial real estate sellers and buyers. For additional information, visit www.MarcusMillichap.com.

data.title: Amazon Sells About $5.74 Billion Worth of Pound-Denominated Notes
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Amazon.com sold notes worth 4.25 billion British pounds sterling, or roughly $5.74 billion.

The notes were due between 2029 and 2045, according to a Monday filing.

The aggregate public offering price of the notes was GBP4.24 billion, and the estimated net proceeds from the offering were roughly the same.

The notes were issued pursuant to an indenture dated in November 2012 and amended in 2022.

data.title: Reborn Coffee, Inc. Q2 2026: Revenue $6.32M, EPS $(0.32) — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Reborn Coffee, Inc. reported second-quarter 2026 results with revenue rising to $6.32M from $1.83M a year earlier, while net loss attributable to Reborn shareholders narrowed to $(2.61M) and basic and diluted net loss per share improved to $(0.32) versus $(1.15) in Q2 2025.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: $6.32M for Q2 2026, up from $1.83M in Q2 2025 (244.6% YoY).
  • Net income: Net loss attributable to Reborn shareholders of $(2.61M) for Q2 2026, versus net loss of $(5.34M) in Q2 2025 (improved YoY).
  • Diluted EPS: Basic and diluted net loss per share $(0.32) for Q2 2026, versus $(1.15) in Q2 2025 (improved YoY).

Business Highlights

  • Revenue growth for the six-month period rose about 227% year-over-year, driven by new service income and licensing expansion.
  • There was a major channel shift to logistics/service income (Reborn Logistics), which became a primary revenue driver.
  • Brand momentum continued with specialty positioning, awards and B2B traction including hotel pour-over pack placements.
  • Operational footprint includes ten retail locations (12 listed including Malaysia) plus a centralized roasting and distribution center.
  • Ongoing R&D and product innovation — including pour-over packs and water/bean processing — are cited as drivers of product differentiation.

Original SEC Filing: Reborn Coffee, Inc. [ REBN ] - 10-Q - Sep. 14, 2026
